recorded: 2026-09-27, gfx1151 Strix Halo (zbook), Gemma 4 26B-A4B Q5_1 expert down-projection grouped prefill
candidate: add a staged variant to the Q5_1 grouped prefill family and prefer it for MoE expert projections. The incumbent launches one block per (expert, out_col) and reloads the expert's whole activation block from L2 once per output column; the staged kernel gives each block a four-column output tile and holds the activation elements a thread needs for the current k-chunk in registers, so one element feeds four outputs. The contraction order is untouched: slot t still accumulates columns t, t + 256, t + 512, ... in increasing order and the tree is still the incumbent's 256-wide stride-128 -> 1 tree, whose first level becomes register-local because a thread owns both slot t and slot t + 128.
reason: the change is bit-exact, so it needs no numerical gate: 0 of 11,534,336 bf16 outputs differ from the incumbent at the model's own down geometry, the route test pins the same 0-difference result at five geometries for Q5_1, and the public path emits 128 of 128 identical greedy token ids. It is therefore promoted to the default path rather than held behind a flag. It is 1.91x on the kernel and 1.161x on the 512/128 prefill row, which makes the down projection no longer the largest remaining prefill cost.

mechanism.structure: one block covers OUT_TILE=4 output columns of one expert with ROW_BATCH=4 and K_TILE=256; the tile shape is the measured optimum of a sweep (row_batch/out_tile of 8/4, 4/4, 4/8, 8/8, 2/4, 2/8, 4/6 at 256, and 4/8 at 512).
mechanism.arithmetic: identical association, not merely close: the k-stride is 256, each slot's column sequence is unchanged, and the reduction is the incumbent's 256-slot tree with its stride-128 level folded into the register pair (value0 + value1) it is equivalent to.
mechanism.refuted_alternative: a wider output tile alone does not help, which is what the existing out8 variant shows: it measures 30.32 ms against the incumbent's 30.99 ms because its inner loop still reloads each activation element once per output column. The columns have to be held across the tile. The K_TILE=512 shape of the same kernel is 17.28 ms but is not bit-exact (11,506,914 of 11,534,336 outputs differ), because a slot's column sequence depends on K_TILE = 256; it was dropped rather than shipped.
mechanism.profile: the incumbent is bandwidth-bound, not instruction-bound: at this geometry it moves ~17 GB in 38.5 ms, 441 GB/s, of which the weight bytes are only 0.3 GB. The staged kernel moves ~3.5 GB in 20.2 ms.
mechanism.refuted_alternative_corrected: The claim that the K_TILE=512 shape 'is not bit-exact because a slot's column sequence depends on K_TILE = 256' gives the wrong reason. The shape is not merely differently associated, it is incomplete: it skips weight blocks 8-15, 36.4% of the contraction. See the correction field.

correctness.gate: not applicable - no arithmetic change, so no execution-profile gate is required
correctness.kernel_level: 0 of 11,534,336 bf16 outputs differ from the incumbent Q5_1 grouped route at in 704 / out 2816 / 128 experts / 4096 compact rows, and 0 of 11,534,336 differ at Qwen4Exp's in 2816 / out 1408 shape.
correctness.unit_test: tests/test_unit_gemma4_expert_route.py::test_grouped_prefill_is_bit_exact_against_the_selected_gemv checks every variant named in _GROUPED_PREFILL_VARIANTS[1:] against the selected GEMV, so the staged variant is covered at (2816, 704), (1408, 2816), (64, 128), (37, 96) and (16, 32). 36 tests pass.
correctness.generation_parity: through LLM.generate() at 512 prompt / 128 output, both arms emit 128 of 128 identical greedy token ids from an identical prompt (sha256 fba226ff8653b8b1).
correctness.route_ran: confirmed rather than inferred: gemma4_moe_grouped_variant_counts() reports the Q5_1 down projection resolving to the staged variant 29 times per 29-layer pass, alongside Q4_K's own staged_out8 29 times, with 58 grouped_prefill projections in total.

correction: CORRECTION (2026-09-27, later unit): the K_TILE=512 shape is not a gate candidate and the 17.28 ms is not a speedup. It is an incomplete kernel. In qwen4_exp_q5_1.hip the staged kernel sets SUBS = K_TILE/32 and its inner loop reads only chunk*SUBS + sub and chunk*SUBS + sub + 4 for sub = threadIdx.x>>5 in 0..3, which is eight 32-wide weight blocks per chunk, while chunks = ceil(in_features/K_TILE). At K_TILE=256 those eight blocks per chunk exactly tile a 256-wide chunk, so three chunks cover all 22 blocks of the 704-wide row (24 slots for 22 blocks, the excess guarded). At K_TILE=512 the chunk is twice as wide but the loop still reads eight blocks, so two chunks read blocks 0-7 and 16-23 and never read blocks 8-15: 256 of 704 columns, 36.4% of the contraction, are skipped. Every output sums over all k, so nearly every output is wrong, which is what the recorded 11,506,914 of 11,534,336 differing outputs (99.76%) shows. The 17.28 ms measures a kernel that does 63.6% of the work, so the apparent 1.17x is an artifact of the omission rather than a faster shape. A correct K_TILE=512 would need the inner loop to iterate SUBS/8 block groups, which is a rewrite rather than an instantiation, and it would still owe a reason to be faster: the accepted row records the staged kernel at ~3.5 GB in 20.2 ms, 173 GB/s, against the incumbent's 441 GB/s, so it is not bandwidth-bound, and the tile sweep already refuted occupancy. The conclusion this field originally drew -- that the route has no remaining bit-exact lever that measurement supports -- stands, and this correction strengthens rather than weakens it.
